chunks: 3089 - Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
If a man purchases his hady and confines it in his house, then it has reached its designated place; so if he wishes, let him shave his head.

key_terms.فَلْيَحْلِقْ: then let him shave his head
key_terms.قَمَطَهُ: confined it or securely bound it
key_terms.هَدْيَهُ: his sacrificial animal offered in the pilgrimage rite

ai.seo_question: When is a sacrificial animal considered to have reached its designated place so that one may shave the head?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sacrificial animal in hajj-related rites. It states that once a man has purchased his hady and secured it in his house, it is treated as having reached its proper destination, after which he may shave his head if he wishes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3089 - Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"If a man purchases his hady (sacrificial animal) and confines it in his house, it has reached its designated place. If he wishes, he may shave his head."
